value.statement: There is an absolute C such that for every finite-support nonnegative ell^2 quadruple y1,y2,y3,y4, sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0)y1(a)y2(b)y3(c)y4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_(j=1)^4||yj||_ell2.

For every contributing nonzero frequency triple r1,r2,r3 with k0=r1+r2+r3!=0 and r1+r2!=0, and phases alpha0=3*r1*r2*(r1+r2), beta0=3*k0*r3*(r1+r2), one has |eta_tau(alpha0,beta0)|/(|k0|*|r1*r2*r3|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird(r1,r2,r3,-k0).

patches.value: For 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, any real base time a, and mean-zero fj in H^sigma, ||R2_(a,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly in a,tau and Fourier support. The bound holds after inserting any multiplier of modulus <=1, including restriction to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. Polynomial approximation defines its unique continuous trilinear extension. Moreover, for 0<gamma<=1, mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f in mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(a,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). This estimate requires no H^gamma bound on f.

For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. H^1 is an algebra: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

Now fix arbitrary continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b] and a third such path h. On k!=0 the coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(r+s=k)exp(-3*i*k*r*s*t)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiation of the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients, so d_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smoothness gives absolute Fourier convergence for every derivative used. Integrate and divide by three to obtain the normal form, summing over pieces if necessary; continuity makes the internal endpoints cancel. Symmetry is immediate. Because Dinv partial_x=P and S_t commutes with these Fourier multipliers, J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}. Integrating gives C_I(f,g,h) with no commutation through a product. At constant f,g the derivative terms vanish, giving Stage=[J]_a^t/6. Quantifying the inputs proves the asserted conclusion.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau from Scheme is a continuous polynomial map from mean-zero L^2 to mean-zero L^2, preserving reality; Ftau maps L^2 continuously to H^1. Smooth data produce smooth iterates. For any trajectory produced by Scheme from smooth mean-zero data, f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, the Interp construction has V(t_n)=f_n, V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), is continuous and piecewise smooth in time and spatially smooth, and has mean-zero values, which are real whenever the initial datum is real. On each open step, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+mathcalR', where mathcalR'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. Thus mathcalR is continuous with the defining increments and the displayed residual identity holds a.e.
periodic input function; smooth in the second paragraph's source application
For every smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), where f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n. Its exact twisted update is f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n).

value.statement: For every smooth exact path u with v=S_(-t)u and smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, if 0<tau<=1 and M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), then every step index j0 with d0=||f_(j0)-v(t_(j0))||_2<=1 satisfies sup_(I_(j0))||rho_(j0)||_2<=C_M*tau*(tau^gamma+d0) and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_(j0);H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+d0).

patches.value: For the forcing term, on each intersected step use the actual residual formula N007: integral J(mathcalR',V)=-C(Y_n,z_n,V)-C(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J(W_n,V). The intervals here are the completed or partial intersection with the step. The first two are O_M(tau*q_n) by N002, putting its negative norm on Y_n, using N008's ||Y_n||_X<=C_M*q_n and ||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_M*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, and N009's bounded V norm on the intersection. H002 and 0<tau<=1 give tau^gamma<=1; since delta_n<=E_I<=1, q_n<=2 and q_n^2<=2*q_n. The last term is O_M(tau*q_n) by N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and the L^2 J bound from N006, since the intersection length is <=tau. Every intersected step starts in I, so delta_n<=E_I. There are at most h/tau+1 such steps. Summing bounds the entire forcing term, also after P_(>N), by C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).
Set Hcut=identity-Lcut, where identity is the identity Fourier operator.

For any three qualifying paths f1,f2,f3, put Lcut=P_(<=N/3), Hcut=identity-Lcut. The trilinear telescoping expansion is C(f1,f2,f3)-C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Lcut f3)=C(Hcut f1,f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Hcut f2,f3)+C(Lcut f1,Lcut f2,Hcut f3). The all-low product has no output above N. Projections contract both parts of X, while ||Hcut fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||fj||_2. In each expanded term apply N002 with the negative norm on its specified high input. Hence ||P_(>N)C_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product||fj||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product||fj||_(L^infty L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e). N009 yields ||e||_X<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I) and bounds the other X norms by C_M; the product of L^2 norms contains E_I. Their total is therefore <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

Choose an integer N>=2 so large that K0*(N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))<=1/4; this is possible because pstar>0. Choose delta=min(1,1/[4*K0*(N^2+3)])>0 and restrict tau<=min(1,delta/2). On any grid-start interval with length h<=delta and E_I<=1, the small-frequency and timestep terms obey K0*(N^2*h+h+tau)<=K0*delta*(N^2+3)<=1/4. N010 therefore absorbs at most half of E_I and yields E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+3*K0*delta*tau^gamma. This estimate includes both endpoints and does not require e(a)=0.

Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. Assume L4: tau<=tau0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time tstar, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,tstar]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(tstar)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. Discharge L4 and L3; this proves the smooth-data estimate, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.

value.declaration: Under L2 let tstar be the asserted first time with error norm one. If any crossing exists, continuity from e(0)=0 supplies such a time.
Let U be the Scheme trajectory from u0 at step tau.
For each m let Um be the Scheme trajectory from u0m at the same tau; U_m^n denotes its nth term.
Choose the constant in N001's two-flow comparison at initial norm sum bound 2*R.

patches.value: H001-H003 give the fixed admissible T,gamma,R. Choose common C,tau0>0 from N011, depending only on these three. Fix arbitrary u0,L and assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma, ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, L is a positive integer and tau=T/L<=tau0. Set u0m=P_(<=m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and the tail of the convergent weighted square sum shows u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L^2. N001 supplies the exact rough solution u and smooth solutions um with a common H^gamma bound. Its two-flow estimate at B0=2R gives sup_[0,T]||um-u||_2<=Kflow||u0m-u0||_2->0.
